summary: All eleven findings confirmed; most fixes need refinements. /1: R_{F̄} for R_F, and /70 as written restates the lemma's hypothesis; /74 should cite Corollary II.5.5. /2: integral TC^gen is Goodwillie's pullback over primes (p. 266); the two missing facts hold, stated for cyclotomic X (the paper's 'p-cyclotomic' on p. 351 is a slip); the KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.4 node cited by the fix is in an unpromoted packet. /3: the counterexample holds; Proposition IV.3.4 and Lemma IV.3.5 need a T-action (a new error, affecting a stated result, not corrected in the Acta correction or v2). /4: RT.2 is the single owner of X^triv; CMM-21's Part II route should be edited to import it, and /137's real overlap is AMMN-22/8, not CMM-21/022. /5: the ∞-category of spectra needs items, but truncations and Eilenberg–MacLane spectra are H.5:spectra's after RS-33, and Mod_HZ ≃ D(Z) is E5:spectra-comparison's; the ∞-category Sp itself is no layer's explicit target (for the maintainer). /6: Mahowald–Hopkins joins LMMT-24's accepted ChromaticHomotopyTheory route, not L.5. /7, /8: confirmed (one more misprint found: C^{BZ} for C^{BT} in Proposition B.19(i)). /9–/11: confirmed.

sources.citation: Acta Math. 221 (2018), 203–409, corrected online version (the text the extraction read).
arXiv v2 and its LaTeX source.

findings.reason: I checked the published page images of pp. 268–270 and p. 276 and the arXiv v2 TeX, which writes \R_{\bar F} and \R_{\bar F_n} throughout. The right adjoint of the shifted-coalgebra functor F̄: CoAlg_F → CoAlg_F is written R_{F̄}. R_F: C → C, introduced on p. 270, is the right adjoint of F. Item /68 gives F̄'s right adjoint the name R_F. Items /69 and /74 write the tower in Proposition II.5.3 and Lemma II.5.10 as … → R_F² → R_F → id (and R_{F_n}), which are endofunctors of C, not of the coalgebra category. Item /70 is false as written. It says R_F sends a coalgebra X → FX to Y = X ×_{R_F F X} R_F X, but R_F(X) is R_F X, not that pullback. For F = Φ^{C_p}, the proof of Theorem II.5.6 on p. 271 has (R_{C_p}X)^{e} ≃ 0, while Y^{e} ≃ X^{e}. Item /70's conclusion, 'the counit F R_F → id is an equivalence', is its own hypothesis: p. 270 says this counit condition 'is equivalent to R_F being fully faithful'. The lemma's actual conclusion is that F̄R_{F̄} → id is an equivalence. Page 272 uses exactly this ('We see from Lemma II.5.4 that Φ̄^{C_p}R_{C̄_p} ≃ id'). The lemma also needs the omitted hypothesis that F preserves pullbacks. The structure map Y → FY needs FY → F R_F X to be an equivalence. That holds only if F preserves the pullback defining Y: then Fη_X is an equivalence by the triangle identity, because the counit is one. The induction in Corollary II.5.5 also uses it. The fix is right, with small refinements. (a) In /70, 'F colimit-preserving' is automatic once F has a right adjoint, so the hypotheses are: C presentable; F has a right adjoint R_F whose counit F R_F → id is an equivalence; F preserves pullbacks. The corollary part should say 'the underlying object of R_{F̄}^k X is R_F^k X ×_{R_F^k F X} … ×_{R_F F X} X'. (b) In /68, write 'F̄ has a right adjoint R_{F̄} with ν: R_{F̄} → id'. (c) In /74, write R_{F̄_n} in the tower and in 'R_{F̄_n}^k X', and keep R_{F_n} for the fully faithful right adjoint of F_n. Cite Corollary II.5.5, not Lemma II.5.4, for the iterated-pullback formula, whose subscripts are R_{F_n}^j F_n X. Medium is acceptable: the paper is right and the items are transcription slips. One could argue for high because /70 is false as stated.

Definition II.4.4 (p. 263) defines only TR(X, p) and TC^gen(X, p). Integral TC^gen(X) is defined on p. 266 by the pullback square (1): TC^gen(X) → X^{hT} over ∏_{p∈P} TC^gen(X, p)_p^∧ → ∏_{p∈P} (X_p^∧)^{hT}. This is a pullback over primes, not a limit over n. Item /60's 'defined by diagram (1) over all n', with locator p. 263, is wrong and does not state the definition. I checked the page image and the TeX. I verified both facts myself. (a) Homotopy fixed points commute with p-completion because S/p is finite, so the right vertical map is X^{hT} → ∏_p (X^{hT})_p^∧, the profinite completion. Its fibre F has F/p ≃ 0 for all p. The pullback therefore gives the left map the same fibre and a profinite-complete target, so it is a profinite completion too. (b) Let X be a bounded below cyclotomic spectrum. Each (X^{tC_ℓ})^{hT} is ℓ-complete (Lemma II.4.2), so its p-completion vanishes for ℓ ≠ p. p-completion is exact and commutes with products. So TC(X)_p^∧ ≃ fib((X_p^∧)^{hT} → (X^{tC_p})^{hT}), and X^{tC_p} ≃ (X_p^∧)^{tC_p} by Lemma I.2.9. X_p^∧ is cyclotomic with φ_ℓ = 0 for ℓ ≠ p, since (X_p^∧)^{tC_ℓ} = 0. Finally Z^{hT} ≃ Z^{hC_{p^∞}} for p-complete Z. Together these give TC(X)_p^∧ ≃ TC(X_p^∧) ≃ TC(X_p^∧, p). I searched all 162 statements and notes. No item contains (a), (b), or the equivalence Z^{hT} ≃ Z^{hC_{p^∞}} for p-complete Z. Item /59 is Lemma II.4.2 and /66 is Theorem II.4.11. Page 352 says (b) 'follows from the discussion in §II.4', and the proof of Proposition IV.3.4 uses 'As TC(X)=TC(X,p)'. One detail in the claim is loose. The proof of Theorem II.4.11 uses (X_p^∧)^{hT} ≃ (X_p^∧)^{hC_{p^∞}} and the commutation of fixed points with completion, to identify the lower row with the p-completed sequences of Theorem II.4.10. It does not use the profinite-completion conclusion itself. The fix is right, with these refinements. (1) In /60, also record footnote 22: this is the corrected form of Goodwillie's definition, learned from Dundas, and taken as the definition. Reference [32] is Dundas–Goodwillie–McCarthy. Optionally split /60 into a p-typical item (p. 263) and an integral item (p. 266). (2) State (b) for bounded below cyclotomic X. On p. 351 the paper writes 'p-cyclotomic', but TC(X) is defined only for cyclotomic spectra (Definition II.1.8), so the item must not copy that. Also state explicitly that Z^{hT} ≃ Z^{hC_{p^∞}} for p-complete Z with T-action. (3) The cross-reference is to KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.4/integral-and-p-typical-tc-agree-after-completion. That node is in a draft packet: there is no accepted decomposition for KTheoryFiniteLocalFields, and the packet's status is partial. So it does not yet 'plan' the result. Record this as a note for the maintainer, and do not edit the draft packet in this fix. Routing the new item as missing with route 1 (RefinedTraceMethods:RT.2) is consistent with how the extraction treats /59.

I checked the published page images of pp. 351–353 and 240–241 and the v2 TeX; the wording is identical. Definition II.1.1(ii) gives a p-cyclotomic spectrum only a C_{p^∞}-action. On p. 351, a Frobenius lift is 'a C_{p^∞}-equivariant factorization'. Proposition IV.3.4 and Lemma IV.3.5 are stated for (p-complete, and for IV.3.4 bounded below) p-cyclotomic spectra, yet they use X^{hT}, ΣX_{hT} and tr. The proof of IV.3.5 starts from 'the T≅T/C_p-equivariant map φ̃_p'. The bridging sentence on p. 352 ('in this case the C_{p^∞}-action on X_p^∧ extends automatically to a T-action') is false for p-cyclotomic spectra, as Remark II.1.3 on pp. 240–241 itself says. I checked the counterexample step by step. Take X = H(F_p[C_{p^∞}]) with C_{p^∞} acting by translation. X is bounded below. It is p-complete: p·id = 0 on an HF_p-module, so the limit of … → X → X under multiplication by p is 0. As a C_p-module, F_p[C_{p^∞}] is free, so X^{tC_p} = 0 and φ_p = 0 is forced. The zero map X → X^{hC_p} is then a C_{p^∞}-equivariant Frobenius lift. BT is simply connected, so any T-action acts trivially on π_*. The restriction to C_{p^∞} would therefore act trivially on π_0 = F_p[C_{p^∞}], but translation does not. So no T-action extends the given one. Strictly, the example shows that the two results are ill-posed on their stated hypothesis class, since X^{hT} and X_{hT} are undefined for it; it does not show that a conclusion is false. The source issue should say so. The Acta correction lists only typesetting fixes, none on pp. 351–354. arXiv v2 is the last version and has the same text. A web search found no other erratum. So known = new is right, and E26 is the next free number. Kind 'error' and affects 'a stated result' are right, because the hypotheses of IV.3.4 and IV.3.5 must change. The E26 entry should add that Theorem IV.3.6 and the rest of the paper are unaffected: (Σ^∞_+LY)_p^∧ has a T-action, and Corollary IV.3.3 gives a T-equivariant lift. It should also quote the p. 351 sentence 'if X is a p-cyclotomic spectrum which is bounded below, then TC(X)_p^∧ = …', since TC(X) is undefined for p-cyclotomic X. This suggests 'cyclotomic' was intended, and under that reading the 'extends automatically' sentence is merely vacuous. The right correction is as follows. For Proposition IV.3.4, take X p-complete and bounded below, with a T-action and a T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant φ_p. By Lemma I.2.9, X^{tC_ℓ} = 0 for ℓ ≠ p, so this is the same as a p-complete bounded below cyclotomic spectrum. It is also the same as a p-cyclotomic spectrum whose C_{p^∞}-action extends to T. Take a Frobenius lift φ̃_p. It may be taken C_{p^∞}-equivariant, because X^{hC_p} and X^{tC_p} are p-complete and, by the full faithfulness in Remark II.1.3, it is then automatically T-equivariant. The conclusion is the pullback with ΣX_{hT} → X, and TC(X) ≃ TC(X, p). For Lemma IV.3.5, only X p-complete with a T-action and a T ≅ T/C_p-equivariant φ̃_p: X → X^{hC_p} is needed; neither bounded below nor φ_p is used. The fix for /124 should keep these two hypothesis sets separate, as the item does now.

Confirmed, with the fix corrected in two places. What I checked. NS18 item /136 states Proposition IV.4.14 (p. 363): -^triv : Sp -> Cyc Sp is left adjoint to TC; the paragraph before it defines X^triv as X with trivial T-action and Frobenius X -> X^{hC_p} -> X^{tC_p}, notes that S^triv is the cyclotomic sphere of Example II.1.2(ii), and derives the adjunction by writing X^triv as the X-indexed colimit of the constant diagram at S^triv. /136 is in NS18 route 1 (source of RefinedTraceMethods:RT.2), which REV-PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18 accepts. CMM-21 item /021 ('Trivial cyclotomic spectra', Definition 2.9) states the same functor and adjunction, more generally: the unique symmetric monoidal colimit-preserving functor Sp -> CycSp, with unit S^triv, left adjoint to TC. It is missing and sits in CMM route 1 (part-ii, RefinedTraceMethodsPartIIHenselianPairs). That route and the paper are both accepted in CMM's review. CMM's brief explicitly tells the design job to 'Cover ... trivial cyclotomic spectra and HF_p^triv'. The queue's make_queue merges every Part II of RefinedTraceMethods into the single pending job DESIGN-RefinedTraceMethodsPartII, which reads that full brief. RT.2 is in the scope of the pending BP-RefinedTraceMethods--RT.1 job, which takes NS18 as a source. So one statement now has two owners. Neither extraction mentions the other. Which owner is right. RT.2 is. Its atlas text defines cyclotomic spectra and constructs TC, TC^- and TP. Everything -^triv is built from already goes to RT.2 through NS18: the cyclotomic sphere /35 (planned RT.2), TC = map(S, -) /40 (planned RT.2), Cyc Sp presentable stable /39 and its symmetric monoidal structure /119 (both routed to RT.2). A Part II starts where RT.2 stops (PROTOCOL section 15), so it imports this. Two corrections to the fix. (1) Apply it; do not only leave a note for the maintainer. The finding's 'where' names the CMM-21 file, so the fixer may edit it. A note would leave the design brief unchanged, and the Part II would plan -^triv again. In CMM-21: make /021 'planned: RefinedTraceMethods:RT.2' and remove it from route 1's items. Rewrite the brief bullet as 'HF_p^triv, with Lemma 2.10, importing -^triv, its symmetric monoidal structure and its adjunction with TC from RT.2', and add -^triv to the brief's 'Import, never re-plan' list for RT.2. In NS18: section 15 asks for the most general form the uses need, so /136 should be restated in CMM's general form: symmetric monoidal, colimit-preserving, unit S^triv (/35), and left adjoint to TC (/40). NS18 uses the monoidality itself, because Corollary IV.4.16 treats HZ_p^triv as an E_infinity-cyclotomic spectrum, and CMM uses HF_p^triv as an E_infinity-algebra in CycSp. Add to /136 a note that CMM-21/021 imports it. (2) Drop the note about /137 overlapping CMM-21/022; that overlap does not hold. /022 concerns HF_p^triv: pi_*(HF_p^{tC_p}) = E(u_{-1}) (x) F_p[t^{+-1}], TC^- = F_p[x], TP = F_p[x^{+-1}], and phi is an isomorphism on pi_0. /137 concerns HZ_p^triv, the shift sh_p and THH(F_p) = sh_p(HZ_p^triv), which are different objects. /022's first clause is the F_p case of NS18 /11 (pi_i HM^{tG} = Tate cohomology, routed to RT.2), and its TC^-/TP clauses are the cohomology of BT with F_p coefficients. The statement that really overlaps /137 is PAPER-ANTIEAU-MATHEW-MORROW-ETAL-22 item /8: a map Z^triv -> THH(F_p) in CycSp, and THH(F_p) = tau_{>=0}(Z^{tC_p}) in Fun(BS^1, Sp). That is exactly the 'in other words' form of Corollary IV.4.16 on p. 364. AMMN-22 puts /8 in its route 2 (a source route to RefinedTraceMethods stages including RT.2). That route is accepted at route level, but AMMN-22's overall verdict is 'revise', so it is not applied yet. The note in /137 should cite AMMN-22/8. The maintainer should keep a single owner for THH(F_p) = tau_{>=0}HZ_p^{tC_p} when AMMN-22 is revised; that is L.5, where NS18's accepted route 5 puts /137. A small factual slip in the claim does not change the verdict. CMM-21 was not 'extracted and accepted a day earlier'. It finished 22 Sept 20:04 UTC, about 15 hours before NS18 (23 Sept 10:58). Its review finished 23 Sept 17:22, about 1.7 hours after NS18's review (15:40). Under section 15 the owner is decided by the layer, not by date. Medium severity stands: without the fix, -^triv is planned twice.

Confirmed, with the planned layers corrected and one item added. The gap. I read all 162 items. None defines or gives a status to the infinity-category Sp, its tensor product and unit S, Sigma^infty_+ -| Omega^infty, the Eilenberg-MacLane functor H, the Postnikov truncations, bounded below spectra or p-completion. The only definition items in this direction are /4 (stable infinity-categories, planned E5:abstract) and the model-level /42-/44 (orthogonal and genuine G-spectra). The report says in prose that 'H.5-H.6 plan spectra, p-completion' and that neither library has spectra, but gives no item. The paper uses all of these throughout. P. 205: 'an E_1-algebra in the infinity-category of spectra Sp in the language of [71]' and 'we write (x)_S for the symmetric monoidal tensor product of spectra'. P. 211, Theorem 1.7: 'if X is bounded below ... identifies T_p(X) with the p-completion of X'. P. 222, Lemma I.2.6 uses tau_{<=n} and tau_{>=-n}. Items /12, /18, /21, /84, /88 and /97 are stated in these terms. PROTOCOL section 16 makes every definition the paper uses an item. Accepted extractions follow this: LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24/1 ('Conventions: spectra, ring spectra and modules', planned H.5:spectra, E5:abstract and E5:presentability) and FENG-GALATIUS-VENKATESH-22/3 (p-completion, planned H.6). So the finding is right. The libraries have none of this. Neither Mathlib 082e2d3 nor Tau Ceti f790474 has spectra in any model. The Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology roadmap excludes spectra in its scope paragraph ('does not include generalized cohomology theories, spectra, bordism'). Mathlib's only truncation is the canonical t-structure on the 1-categorical derived category (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t, Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/TStructure.lean:34), which is not what NS18 uses. So the new items are 'planned', not 'library'. Corrections to the fix. (b) Postnikov truncations of spectra are not EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2. E2 builds truncations and Postnikov towers of derived categories of sheaves. The accepted RS-33 narrows H.5:spectra to keep 'Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra from chain complexes, their homotopy/cohomology comparison and functorial truncations'. The confirmed RT-AREA-ktheory-1/16 puts the same targets in H.5:spectra. So plan H and tau_{<=n}, tau_{>=n} in H.5:spectra. Plan Postnikov convergence (Y = lim tau_{<=n}Y and colim tau_{>=-n}Y = Y, the input to Lemma I.2.6, /18) in H.6, which RS-33 makes the owner of spectrum towers, Milnor sequences and convergence. (a) The smash product is H.5:spectra's after RS-33, which moved generic smash out of H.5:S-delooping. (d) Add one more item: Mod_{HZ}(Sp) = D(Z), with its HZ_p variant. /134, /138 and footnote 9 use it ('X in D(Z)^{BT}', 'for HZ-module spectra'). The E5 packet's E5:spectra-comparison node plans it as 'the Eilenberg-Mac Lane comparison'. (c) As the finding says, bounded below spectra and p-completion go to H.6. The ordering point is real and is the reason for medium severity. From NS18's first chapter on, RT.2 needs Sp as a presentably symmetric monoidal stable infinity-category. Sp^{BG}, colimits and limits over BG, and the lax symmetric monoidal Tate construction (/22, /29) cannot be built on a stable homotopy category. In the atlas, RT.2's only stage prerequisite is RT.1, which is fed by H.5:spectra and E5:abstract. There is no edge from E5:presentability, even though NS18 /5 and /6 are planned there, and none from E5:spectra-comparison, which its own stage text calls a late return. The E5 packet node E5:spectra-comparison/late-realisation says the construction of Sp 'is StableHomotopyKTheory's by the roadmap's division, and this layer only compares'. But H.5:spectra plans only a concrete model and a stable homotopy category. So the presentably symmetric monoidal infinity-category Sp is no layer's explicit target. That E5 packet is still a draft (REV-EnhancedDerivedSheaves--E5 is pending). An extraction has no 'requests' field, so put this in the new item's note and in the report for the maintainer. Ask that H.5:spectra export the symmetric monoidal presentable infinity-category of its model early, for example by the symmetric monoidal Dwyer-Kan localisation of NS18 /140, and that E5:presentability -> RT.2 be added.

Confirmed, with the routing of the Mahowald-Hopkins item corrected. (a) Footnote 9 (p. 219, on Example I.2.3): 'One can, however, check that they hold for all chain complexes, as then both (X_{hC_p})^{t(C_{p^2}/C_p)} and (X^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p^2}/C_p)} are modules over the E_infinity-ring spectrum (HZ^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p^2}/C_p)} = 0.' No item has it: /12 assumes bounded below, /13 bounded above, /19 covers HM only, and no note mentions the footnote. I checked the argument. For X in Fun(BC_{p^2}, Mod_HZ), X^{hC_p} and X_{hC_p} are modules over HZ^{hC_p}, compatibly with the residual action. The residual Tate construction is lax symmetric monoidal (/29), so their Tate constructions are modules over (HZ^{hC_p})^{t(C_{p^2}/C_p)}. That ring vanishes by the Tate fixpoint lemma, since HZ is bounded above. So the statement holds for every X in D(Z)^{BC_{p^2}}. It is what /138 needs: THH(A) is an HZ_p^triv-module, hence an HZ-module with T-action, and p. 365 says 'for HZ-module spectra, the Tate orbit lemma is always valid'. Routing it to RT.2 with /12, /13 and /19 is right. Add one point to the fix. /138 also needs Lemma II.4.1 in the form 'for every X satisfying the Tate orbit lemma'. The paper states that form on p. 220, and the proof on p. 261 uses nothing else. But /58 and /59 are stated only for bounded below X. So note in /58 that the proof needs only the orbit-lemma conclusion, and note in /138 that p-completeness is automatic, because p is nullhomotopic on any THH(HF_p)-module. (b) Mahowald-Hopkins, Remark IV.4.5 (p. 357): '(i) The free E_2-algebra in Sp with a chosen nullhomotopy p=0 is given by HF_p.' It is used on p. 364: 'Fixing a nullhomotopy from p to 0, we get that A is an E_2-HF_p-algebra, by Remark IV.4.5.' It appears only in the note of /130. I checked the wording point. Freeness gives exactly an E_2-ring map HF_p -> A. THH is symmetric monoidal (/119), so this becomes an E_1-algebra map THH(HF_p) -> THH(A) in Cyc Sp. That makes THH(A) a left THH(HF_p)-module, and through the E_infinity map HZ_p^triv -> THH(HF_p) an HZ_p^triv-module, which is all the argument uses. An E_2-algebra in Mod_{HF_p} would need more (an E_3 map to the E_2-centre). So writing 'an E_2-ring map HF_p -> A (Mahowald-Hopkins)' in /138 is correct and costs nothing. The routing in the fix is wrong. Do not route the new Mahowald-Hopkins item 'with /138' to KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.5. The accepted LAND-MATHEW-MEIER-ETAL-24 extraction already assigns this theorem to the new roadmap ChromaticHomotopyTheory. Its item /78 says HF_p is the Thom spectrum of the E_2-map Omega^2 S^3 -> BGL_1(S_p^) sending the generator to 1-p, 'by a theorem of Mahowald for p = 2 and Hopkins for odd p'. That item is in its accepted new route, whose brief lists 'Mahowald's and Hopkins's theorem identifying the colimit as HF_p'; DESIGN-ChromaticHomotopyTheory is pending. NS18's form (i) is the equivalent universal-property form, as the paper says ('Equivalently', since Omega^2 S^3 is the free E_2-group on S^1). Under section 15, the NS18 item should join that roadmap through a 'new' route to ChromaticHomotopyTheory, the way CMM-21 joined ArcTopologyAndDescent. Ask that the roadmap also state form (i), and have /138 cite the item. On prerequisites: [16] Blumberg and [17] Blumberg-Cohen-Schlichtkrull are the paper's references for deducing Boekstedt periodicity from Mahowald-Hopkins, so they belong with /130. They are not sources for the theorem itself; LMMT-24/78 already cites Mahowald and Antolin-Camarena-Barthel for that. Minor: /138's locator should be pp. 364-365, since the fibre sequence and the [v^{-1}] formula are on p. 365. Low severity is right.

All three parts check out at their locators in the published text, and the TeX of arXiv v2 reads the same. (a) Item /104 gives no hypothesis on R. /103 carries the properness clause, but /104 does not. On p. 315 the paper deduces that Φ_p is an underlying equivalence 'by Proposition III.5.5 and Theorem III.4.7'. Propositions III.5.5 and III.5.6 identify the source and target of Φ_p with realisations of Λ_p^op-orthogonal spectra. Construction III.4.6 gives a map between them, and Theorem III.4.7 (pp. 308–310, no hypotheses) says this map is a stable equivalence in each degree. To go from a stable equivalence in each degree to one on the naive realisation, you need the simplicial objects to be proper (Reedy h-cofibrant). This is Proposition B.15 and Corollary B.16, and the proof of Proposition C.11 uses the same argument. The paper says this itself on p. 312: 'According to Corollary B.16, we have to verify that THH(R; X) is proper'. It then proves properness only in Lemma III.5.2, for R levelwise well pointed with S⁰ → R_0 an h-cofibration. Remark III.5.3 declines to prove the weaker version ('we will not prove this slightly more general result here'). Footnote 4 on p. 206 also presents this basepoint condition as the standing requirement of the classical construction. So the paper's argument supports /104 only under Lemma III.5.2's hypotheses, which the paper tacitly assumes throughout §III.5. The fix is right: add the hypothesis to /104 as Theorem III.6.1 (/105) already has it, with a note that §III.5 assumes it tacitly (pp. 312, 206). No sourceIssue is needed, because the paper names the condition before it uses it. (b) Definition II.3.6, p. 259 (arXiv v2 TeX: the same square). The top-left corner is Φ^{C_n}_U(Φ^{C_m}_U X), with the arrow ≃ to Φ^{C_mn}_U X and then Φ_{mn}. The left column is Φ^{C_n}_U(Φ_m) followed by Φ_n. /55 writes Φ_{mn} ∘ (Φ^{C_m}_U Φ^{C_n}_U X ≃ Φ^{C_mn}_U X) = Φ_n ∘ Φ^{C_n}_U(Φ_m). The two sides of this equation then start from different objects, Φ^{C_m}Φ^{C_n}X and Φ^{C_n}Φ^{C_m}X. The two objects are isomorphic, but the equation as written does not type-check. The red team's corrected formula is exactly the paper's square. (c) The sentence before Proposition B.19 on p. 394 reads: 'Using the functor sd_p: Λ_p → Λ, we get for every cyclic object X a subdivided Λ_p-object sd_p^*X'. So in B.19 the operation sd_p^* is pullback along Λ_p → Λ, which is defined on cyclic objects. Also, the realisation of a paracyclic space carries only an R-action (Construction B.9). A T-action exists only for cyclic spaces (Corollary B.14), so the claim of a 'T-equivariant homeomorphism' makes sense only for cyclic X. The paper defines 'proper' for cyclic spaces on p. 391 ('a cyclic space is called proper if the underlying simplicial space is'), and the paper uses B.19 only for cyclic objects: the THH cyclic object in §III.2, and THH(R) in §III.5 (pp. 313–314, the proof of Proposition III.5.4). So 'proper cyclic' is what the paper means. One wording point: the red team says 'sd_p^* is only defined on cyclic objects', which is too strong. The paper also builds an endofunctor sd_p: Λ_∞ → Λ_∞ (p. 392), along which paracyclic objects can be pulled back. The operation in B.19 is the one on Λ_p → Λ, however, and the T-equivariance argument is decisive, so the conclusion stands. The fix for /155 is right: write 'proper cyclic spaces or spectra', and record the misprint as finding 8 does.

I checked all five mistakes. Each is in the published text and in arXiv v2, the Acta correction lists none of them, and none is among E1–E25. (1) Proof of Corollary I.4.3, p. 238 (arXiv v2 PDF line 'commutes with Postnikov limits as in Lemma I.2.6 (ii)'; the TeX has Lemma~\ref{lem:tateconvergence}~(ii)). The next sentence reads 'Thus, by taking the limit over all τ_{≤n}X'. Commuting with lim_n τ_{≤n} is Lemma I.2.6(i) (p. 222). Part (ii) is about colim_n τ_{≥−n}. The claim itself is true: (s_!X)_{hC_n} ≃ X ⊗ (T/C_n)_+ commutes with all limits. So the only slip is the part number. (2) Proof of Theorem III.4.7, p. 310. On the page image (PDF page 108) the text reads 'n_V = min_{H⊊V}(…)' and 'for varying H⊊V', and the v2 TeX has \min_{H\subsetneq V} twice. The case split just above (p. 309, and TeX 'If H\subsetneq C_p') runs over subgroups H of C_p, while V is a representation, so the intended text is H ⊊ C_p. (3) Proposition B.19(ii), p. 395: 'For a proper paracyclic topological space (resp. spectrum) X, there is a natural T-equivariant homeomorphism |X| ≅ |sd_p^*X|'. The same wording is in v2. It should read 'proper cyclic', for the reasons given under finding 7(c). (4) Footnote 46, p. 389 (page image checked; the TeX is the same). The text sets f(1/(n+1)) = min t^{-1}(R≥0) and makes f(k/(n+1)) the successor of f((k−1)/(n+1)) for 1 ≤ k ≤ n. The case k = 1 says that f(1/(n+1)) is the successor of f(0), so f(0) is the predecessor of min t^{-1}(R≥0). I checked this against the illustration the footnote itself recommends, using T ≅ (1/n)Z with the minimum sent to 0. Then f(k/(n+1)) = (k−1)/n for 1 ≤ k ≤ n, f(0) = −1/n, and f(1) = f(0)+1 = (n−1)/n = f(n/(n+1)). This map is non-decreasing and Z-equivariant. The footnote's 'f(0) is the successor' would give f(0) > f(1/(n+1)), so it should say predecessor, or equivalently 'min t^{-1}(R≥0) is the successor of f(0)'. This is a different slip from E17, which is about display (20) on the same page. (5) Proof of Proposition A.14, p. 378 (page image checked; v2 the same): '…and a transformation G′_1F → G′_0'. In M(φ) = X_1 ∪_{X_0×{1}} X_0×Δ¹ (p. 376), the edge 0 → 1 makes a functor out of M(φ) the same as G′_0 on X_0×{0}, G′_1 on X_1, and a transformation G′_0 → G′_1F. On p. 377, functors out of M(φ′) correspond to 2-cells G_0 → G_1∘LF. By the universal property of the right Kan extension G_1∘LF, maps into it correspond to transformations G_0 i_0 → G_1 i_1 F, which is G′_0 → G′_1F. So the printed direction is reversed. E23 concerns the typesetting of the p. 377 diagram (which the correction reprints), not this sentence, and the corrected online text still has G′_1F → G′_0.
